question.problem:
In **ascending order**,  the exact solutions in radians to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$ are

${x}_{1}=$
{{field-1}}$,\,{x}_{2}=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
We divide both sides of the equation by $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1)=\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the other solution in the given interval, we add $\pi $ to the principal value. Hence,

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{4}+\pi =\frac{5\pi }{4}.
$$

So, in ascending order, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{4},\,{x}_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{4}.
$$
